text:
sam_sales: Heads up — FinTrust POC blocked. Their app resolves our private endpoint but every request returns 403 AccessDenied. Demo is tomorrow, need quick triage.
eli_engineer: Do you have the exact curl and the service principal/role they're using? 403 usually means auth at the endpoint layer or header/token mangling.
marta_netops: Confirming DNS -> they see 10.1.2.33 which is our interface endpoint in their VPC. If this is cross-account, endpoint resource policy must allow their role/arn.
sam_sales: They used an app Role arn:aws:iam::876543210987:role/fintrust-poc-role. They also said traffic passes through a corporate TLS-proxy. Here is the sanitized curl: 

```
curl -v https://api.internal.redwood/v1/ping \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  --resolve api.internal.redwood:443:10.1.2.33
```

Response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"AccessDenied","message":"principal not authorized for endpoint"}
```
eli_engineer: Two hypotheses: 1) VPC Endpoint policy doesn't include their role, so endpoint accepts TCP but denies. 2) Proxy is doing TLS intercept (MITM) — SNI or client headers lost so downstream mapping fails.
kevin_sre: Ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.1.2.33:443 -servername api.internal.redwood` and paste the certificate issuer. If it shows their corp CA, proxy is re-signing. If it shows our cert, probs endpoint policy.
juno_security: Also validate JWT claims: `iss` and `org_id` must match what our auth layer expects. Proxies sometimes strip or reissue Authorization headers.
marta_netops: I'll send the minimal VPCE policy snippet we recommend for cross-account POCs: 

```
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::876543210987:role/fintrust-poc-role"},
      "Action":"*",
      "Resource":"*"
    }
  ]
}
```

If they used an EC2 instance principal instead of the app role, it would fail like this.
sam_sales: They're saying ops configured the endpoint with `Principal: *` but added a condition restricting `aws:SourceVpc` to their corp VPC — could that block calls from their app running in a different VPC or pod network?
eli_engineer: Yes, that condition can block cross-VPC traffic. Also check whether `aws:SourceVpce` is used incorrectly.
kevin_sre: If proxy is unavoidable, options: 1) get proxy to allow TLS passthrough to 10.1.2.33; 2) use a temporary SSH tunnel from a bastion in their VPC to test; 3) enable mutual TLS for the endpoint (requires client cert onboarding). For immediate demo, fastest is updating endpoint policy to explicitly allow their role and ensure no restrictive conditions.
devops-bot: run vpce:validate-policy vpce-0f12a3b4 started
sam_sales: I'll ask them for the openssl output and the endpoint policy JSON. Also asked product ops for a 2-week POC pricing quote in case we need dedicated routing.
juno_security: If they want a long POC with corp proxy, we should document cert pinning and token claim expectations for their security reviewers.
marta_netops: I'll standby to review their endpoint policy once they paste it.
kevin_sre: TL;DR next steps for customer: 1) run openssl s_client and paste cert issuer; 2) paste endpoint policy JSON (sanitized); 3) confirm which IAM principal the app actually uses at runtime; 4) check proxy does not strip Authorization.
sam_sales: Thanks all — looping FinTrust in and will update.
